The Claude Code bird ages only while you work, and the day turns at your midnight.

## The minutes are the ones you worked

The README's first promise is that a gap longer than five minutes is a break
and does not count. It was true above a shell prompt and false in Claude Code,
where the session JSON offers only a wall clock: a window left open all
afternoon aged the bird as if you had typed all afternoon. The status line now
reads the transcript's own timestamps, turn by turn and tool call by tool call,
and keeps a small ledger per session (`~/.canary/active`) of the minutes that
were actually work. A repaint credits nothing. The first refresh after this
upgrade starts that count from what the transcript's tail shows, so a long
session may show fewer minutes than it did a moment before; they are the true
ones.

## The day is yours, not Greenwich's

Daily peaks, the night streak and "the seventh session of a day" were keyed on
UTC days. In Rome the day turned at 02:00, so a session from 23:00 to 03:00
was two days, and its peak came back as debt onto itself after two. Days now
turn at local midnight.

## A night past the limit means past it

The history counted a day that peaked at exactly 90 as a night past your
limit, while 90 scores as worn, the band that means stop, and dead starts at
91. A streak could begin on nights that were never dead. And tonight's count
extended the streak on the score after debt, while the file remembered the
raw peak: "✕ 3 nights" tonight became two by morning. Both count the same
thing now, the raw peak past 90.

## The body clock credits the right hour

In Claude Code the awake-hours histogram was told the hour had turned by a
repaint, credited 14:00 with turns typed at 13:xx, and had nothing left for
the first real turn of the afternoon. It follows the turns now, and credits
the hour they happened in.

## The installer signs off on what it did

A source build that failed still returned success and reported the status
line wired, with the old binary in place. It now says the build failed and
exits non-zero. Every path builds or downloads beside the destination and
renames into place, so a bird running mid-install gets the old one or the new
one, never half. And `sh install.sh` from inside the checkout builds from
source, as the README said; it used to download, because a bare script name
has no slash in it.

## The plugin

Claude Code keeps its copy of the plugin without `.git`, so a build from it
said `canary dev`. The installer now takes the version from the plugin
manifest there, which release CI holds equal to the tag. The plugin's hook
keeps the binary at the installer's own path (`~/.local/bin/canary`) at the
plugin's version, so `/plugin update` moves the bird along; one from Homebrew
or `go install` lives elsewhere and is never touched. The hook fetches the
release binary rather than building one, because a `go build` inside Claude
Code's start-up behind a slow module proxy is a stall with no visible cause.
And it says so when it leaves a `settings.json` alone, instead of staying
quiet about a status line that never appeared.
